data.narrative:
Dragonfly Aerospace, a Series G frontier-tech company in Space & Aerospace founded by Bryan Dean, has raised $20M to date. The sector peer universe comprises 5 public comps (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, and Planet Labs, though narrow same-stage filtering yielded insufficient datapoints for reliable peer-median anchoring.

Only the stage-progression method was applicable. Using total raised ($20M) as a proxy base and applying a 1.25x multiplier typical of Series G advancement, the analysis implies a valuation of $51M. This reflects the step-up observed as capital deployment and operational scale increase between institutional rounds at this maturity level. The public Space & Aerospace sector median trades at 24.4x P/S across six tickers, but revenue data for Dragonfly is unavailable, precluding direct multiple application.

The triangulated range spans $44M (low) to $59M (median $51M), derived entirely from the single applicable method. Key uncertainties include revenue trajectory, which would enable public-comp anchoring, and the absence of same-stage private comparables to validate stage-progression assumptions. The narrow methodological foundation argues for sensitivity around competitive positioning, unit economics, and path to revenue. Further diligence on burn rate and runway would refine this estimate.
